 11:29 (IST) Oct 25 The sacred festivals of Diwali and Chhath are just a few days away. Cleanliness campaigns are being run from place to place. It's important that we keep those places clean where we live.
 PM Modi
 11:28 (IST) Oct 25 ‘Taking our products to markets around the world’: PM Modi on Vocal for Local in Mann Ki Baat Addressing the 139th Episode of Mann Ki Baat, Prime Minister Narendra Modi says, "During this festive season, you must all have noticed a change around you. Now people have started giving a lot of importance to indigenous products while shopping. This spirit of 'Vocal for Local' is taking our products to markets around the world." 11:21 (IST) Oct 25 ‘Breathe new life into a river’: PM Modi on Heval revival in Mann Ki Baat Addressing the 139th Episode of Mann Ki Baat, Prime Minister Narendra Modi says, "In the Tehri Garhwal region of Uttarakhand, people have come together in an effort to breathe new life into a river—the 'Heval'. Some time ago, the water level in the Heval River began to decline, and nearby natural water sources were also drying up. In response, the local administration and the villagers joined forces to launch a campaign to save the river. During this initiative, measures were taken to capture rainwater, facilitate groundwater recharge, and plant a large number of trees. Today, as a result of these efforts, the Heval River has been revitalized, and dozens of natural water sources have also been restored." Join conversation

 10:54 (IST) Oct 25 Polls open for presidential election in Bulgaria dominated by economic hardship and Ukraine war Bulgarians are heading to the polls Sunday to elect their next president in a campaign centered on growing economic hardship and drone attacks on Black Sea shipping.
 The vote will also be the first major test for the Moscow-friendly Progressive Bulgaria party of Prime Minister Rumen Radev after its election triumph in April.
 Despite a record number of candidates, the race is expected to be decided in a runoff between incumbent President Iliana Yotova, backed by Radev’s party, and former caretaker Prime Minister Andrey Gyurov, who is backed by pro-Western opposition parties.

 Lite Challenge Play Now 10:09 (IST) Oct 25 Rahul Gandhi should understand role of LoP: Raghunandan Rao questions INDIA bloc’s rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan 08:48 (IST) Oct 25 Delhi: Fire breaks out in Rani Garden shanties; belongings gutted, no casualties reported A fire broke out in shanties in Rani Garden, under the jurisdiction of Geeta Colony Police Station in the national capital, on Sunday, officials said.
 No injuries or casualties were reported in the incident, although several hutments and household belongings were reduced to ashes.
 "The cause of the fire is still under investigation. We arrived at the scene and immediately began firefighting operations, bringing the blaze under control within half an hour. No injuries have been reported," the Fire Officer said.
 Recounting the incident, an affected resident said they were asleep when the fire broke out and lost all their household belongings in the blaze.
 "I don’t know how the fire started; we were just sleeping, and everything burned down. Nothing is left—everything was destroyed. I’m only left with the clothes I’m wearing. Thankfully, no one was hurt—the children are safe. Everything else, all our belongings, burned to ashes," the resident said.
 08:42 (IST) Oct 25 LPG distributors' body opposes Delhi protest, indefinite strike, urges uninterrupted supply The FLDI does not support the proposed protests and indefinite strike in Delhi. We advocate for meaningful dialogue, concrete decisions, and sustained efforts to address the legitimate demands of distributors. We are engaged in constructive dialogue with the Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) and the Ministry of Petroleum. The concerns of the distributors are being heard, and we have received assurances of an early resolution. We believe that solutions can be achieved through dialogue and decisive action. Ensuring uninterrupted LPG service to consumers is our top priority. Dialogue with the OMCs and the Ministry is ongoing, and we have been assured of a resolution. Given this, resorting to protests without exhausting all avenues for dialogue is not a practical approach. Maintaining a regular and safe supply of LPG to consumers remains our primary objective. We urge all fellow distributors to continue with supply and delivery operations—ignoring unverified calls for action—so that no family faces any inconvenience: Federation of LPG Distributors of India 08:19 (IST) Oct 25 Earthquake of magnitude 6.16 strikes Vanuatu islands, GFZ says 08:19 (IST) Oct 25 Japan's Bonin Islands region hit by 6.3 magnitude earthquake, says EMSC 07:45 (IST) Oct 25 Soldiers guard centre of Milan as thousands of protesters march in cities across Europe Thousands of young people marched on Saturday through the streets of several Italian cities, including Milan, Rome and Turin, as authorities deployed large numbers of police and soldiers in a largely-successful bid to stave off a repeat of the violent clashes and looting that marred similar protests last week.
 The demonstration in Milan remained peaceful, but there were brief clashes with police in both Rome and Turin.
 In Milan, thousands of young people marched the streets as soldiers were deployed and luxury boutiques were boarded up, but by late afternoon, most shops had opened, Italian media reported.
 Premier Giorgia Meloni announced a raft of measures, including sending an additional 500 soldiers to Milan and tougher penalties for minors, who police said made up a large part of the violent protesters last week. In Milan, police detained several minors as a preventive measure, media reported.
 While protests in France have claimed most international attention, large demonstrations also rocked many European cities on Saturday from Milan to Rome to Madrid, Lisbon and Tirana.
 The protests encompass a broad range of issues from education and corruption to anti-war movements, pensions and housing.
 04:38 (IST) Oct 25 Fire breaks out at Quaker Oats plant in Cedar Rapids, Iowa A fire broke out Saturday at a Quaker Oats plant in Iowa. There were no immediate reports of injuries.
 The Cedar Rapids Fire Department said firefighters responded to the call at about 4:45 p.m. Video and photos posted to social media showed black smoke over the downtown of the city of about 140,000.
 There was no immediate information on what caused the fire. 
 PepsiCo Foods US said in a statement that fire responders went to the scene of the blaze and how it started would be investigated.
 The Quaker Oats brand, by way of the Quaker Mill Company, turns 150 years old in 2027. It is owned by PepsiCo.
 The Quaker Oats facility is the largest milling facility in the world, processing over 2 million pounds (900,000 kilograms) of oats daily, according to the company’s website.
 00:08 (IST) Oct 25 Manipur: Security forces arrest 17 suspected militants, seize large cache of weapons Security forces in Manipur on Saturday arrested 17 suspected militants belonging to two Kuki outfits for allegedly impersonating registered cadres under the Suspension of Operations (SoO) agreement signed with the Centre in August 2008. 
 A police official said a joint operation involving Manipur Police, the Quick Action Team of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) and the Commando Battalion for Resolute Action (CoBRA) was conducted at Sinai Camp, a designated SoO camp of the Kuki National Organisation (KNO)/Kuki National Army (KNA) and KNO/Kuki Liberation Army (KLA) outfits. 
 The official said that during the verification process, 17 cadres were found to be impersonating registered SoO cadres by using false identities. 
 Of the 17 accused, eight were allegedly impersonating KNA cadres and nine KLA cadres. All of them were subsequently arrested. 
 Security personnel also recovered and seized more than 24 firearms, 38 magazines, a large quantity of ammunition, explosives, wireless communication equipment and other combat gear during the operation. (IANS)
 00:06 (IST) Oct 25 CM Adityanath reviews preparations for air show scheduled for Sunday in Varanasi Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath reviewed preparations for the air show scheduled for Sunday during a meeting with officials at the Circuit House auditorium here, the UP government said in a statement.
 Emphasising the need to ensure easy public access to the Ganga ghats, he directed officials to avoid unnecessary barricading.
 In view of the expected heavy crowds, he stressed that adequate attention must be paid to public convenience alongside security arrangements.
 The chief minister also directed officials to ensure proper cleanliness along all major roads and at event venues across the city.
 He said, "Additional cleaning at all Ganga ghats, adequate toilet facilities and the availability of drinking water must be ensured to prevent any inconvenience to spectators." (PTI)
 00:05 (IST) Oct 25 Power bank triggers fire in ladies' coach of Mumbai local train; no injuries A power bank exploded inside a passenger’s bag in a ladies’ compartment of a Mumbai local train, triggering panic among commuters, railway officials said on Saturday.
 No one was injured in the incident that occurred around 12.30 pm on Friday on a Badlapur-bound local train from Dadar.
 A Central Railway (CR) spokesperson said a woman’s bag caught fire following a suspected power bank explosion before the train reached Ghatkopar station. Thick smoke filled the compartment, prompting passengers to pull the alarm chain.
 Alert commuters removed the burning bag and extinguished the fire with water.
 While nobody was injured, the female commuter’s belongings were destroyed, the official said.
 The train was halted at Ghatkopar station between 12.51 pm and 12.53 pm for safety checks. Railway staff inspected the train before it resumed its journey, the official added. (PTI)
 00:04 (IST) Oct 25 Indian envoy meets Sri Lanka’s Agriculture minister, inaugurates India-backed Model Village in Galle India's High Commissioner to Sri Lanka Santosh Jha met the country's Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation, K.D. Lal Kantha, for a conversation on politics, agricultural innovation and international geopolitical developments, the Envoy said on Saturday.
 "Pleasure to meet K.D. Lal Kantha, Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation for a conversation on politics, agricultural innovation and international geopolitical developments," High Commissioner Santosh Jha said on social media platform X.
 The Envoy also met the leadership of Sri Lanka's Women's Chamber of Industry and Commerce (WCIC), led by its Chairperson Gayani De Alwis, and described women's entrepreneurship as an essential pillar of economic growth for both countries.
 "Delighted to meet the leadership of Women's Chamber of Industry and Commerce, (WCIC) led by its Chairperson Gayani De Alwis. Women entrepreneurship is an essential pillar for economic growth and prosperity for both India and Sri Lanka. Was very happy to hear about WCIC's strong and growing partnerships with India," Jha said in another post.
 00:04 (IST) Oct 25 Protests sweep Italian cities amid heavy security presence, some violence reported Protests against war and rising living costs took place in major Italian cities on Saturday, with some incidents of violence, a week after unrest erupted across the country.
 Authorities deployed a heavy police presence and many shops closed as a precaution against possible damage.
 The demonstrations, which followed clashes last weekend in which protesters fought with police, looted shops and vandalised property, were violent in Turin, Rome and Bologna, with clashes between officers and demonstrators. They were largely peaceful in Milan.
 Reuters witnesses did not observe any shops being looted or property vandalised.
 After calls for further demonstrations circulated on social media this week, authorities made extensive security arrangements and deployed large numbers of police officers to prevent a repeat of last weekend's violence.
 Earlier on Saturday, Italian police said they had detained a person allegedly linked to organising the "October 17 Movement" — last weekend's protests — and had taken them to police headquarters in Milan for questioning. (Reuters)
